header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Michael Zhang (AcmeCorp Head of Security), Laura Perez (AcmeCorp Procurement Manager), Daniel Kim (AcmeCorp CTO), Amira Soliman (AcmeCorp Legal)
summary: Procurement/legal review covering Redwood MSA & DPA, SLAs, security artifacts (SOC2, ISO), KMS/encryption, data residency, pricing structure for dedicated vs hosted, and onboarding/POC next steps. Action items assigned for delivering redlines, compliance docs, and scheduling POC.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i see folks on the line, we'll kick off, just a quick agenda — legal review, slas, pricing, p o c timelines, and next steps.
[00:12] Laura: thanks Jordan, yeah from procurement side we want to make sure the MSA and DPA match our standard terms, especially around indemnity and data retention.
[00:20] Jordan: totally, and Amira from legal is on as well so we can capture specific redlines. Priya, do you want to add anything on technical constraints?
[00:28] Priya: sure — hi all — technical items that usually come up: data residency, encryption at rest/in transit (KMS/HSM), SSO via SAML, audit logs, and optionally private deployment (VPC). we also want to clarify any exposure from caching, kv cache behavior, and retention windows.
[00:42] Michael: yep, security team will look at SOC2 report and keys. two ques right away: 1) can we use our own KMS? 2) is there a way to ensure logs go to our SIEM?
[00:52] Jordan: short answers — yes on customer-managed KMS for Private deployment and we can stream audit logs or provide export; specifics in the security pack. i'll send the SOC2 and the compliance pack after the call.
[01:01] Amira: on the DPA, we have a few required clauses around subprocessor lists and notification timelines for breaches — any standard timelines you commit to? 72 hours? 24 hours?
[01:10] Jordan: typical is 72 hours for initial notification; we can discuss escalation for certain data classes. also we have options for stricter SLA-backed responses on Dedicated tier.
[01:20] Daniel: on SLAs — Acme is sensitive to latency for customer-facing features. what uptime and latency SLAs do you offer for hosted vs dedicated?
[01:30] Priya: hosted api has a best-effort <99.9% guideline but without enterprise SLA; Dedicated has a contractual 99.95% uptime with latency SLOs we'd agree per route — for example P95 token latency targets depend on model and sequence length. exact numbers go in the SLA exhibit.
[01:45] Michael: and for the pilot, will the traffic run on hosted or dedicated? procurement prefers hosted for speed, security prefers private/dedicated.
[01:54] Samir: we usually recommend starting the pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity if you need predictable latency and isolation, but we can do an initial functional pilot on hosted and then move to Dedicated for scale.
[02:05] Laura: pricing question — can you outline pricing differences between hosted, dedicated reserved, and private on-prem? we need to budget.
[02:12] Jordan: yes. hosted is usage-based per token/embedding, no commit. Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity fee (committed GPUs) plus overage; Private (on-prem) is licensing + support. i'll send a pricing sheet that lays out sample monthly costs for expected qps.
[02:25] Priya: to add — Optimize tooling can reduce token costs via caching, batching, and quantization recommendations, we'll show estimated unit economics in the POC spreadsheet.
[02:33] Michael: about audit — will you provide logs with token-level cost breakdown? also retention controls so we can purge dataset after X days?
[02:41] Jordan: yes, we have token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console, and retention is configurable. DPA will cover deletion at customer request and retention defaults; we can add a stricter retention clause for Acme.
[02:53] Amira: On indemnity and liability caps — we usually push for standard caps that exclude willful misconduct; any negotiation room?
[03:00] Jordan: typical enterprise redlines are accommodated; we prefer dollar-cap models tied to fees but open to reasonable negotiation — legal team will review and propose language.
[03:10] Laura: procurement timeline — we aim to complete legal review and sign by end of month if we get redlines this week.
[03:17] Jordan: understood. we'll aim to get redlined MSA+DPA to you by friday.
[03:22] Priya: quick technical clarifications: do you need VPC peering or a private endpoint? and what RTO for key rotations?
[03:30] Daniel: VPC peering preferred; we'll share network contact. for key rotation we have key rotations monthly and need to ensure KMS integration supports our key policy.
[03:38] Priya: ok noted — for VPC we support private control plane options; will follow up with network checklist.
[03:44] Michael: another security note — can we run a small benchmark for latency at peak qps? want to validate P95 under load.
[03:51] Priya: yes, we'll include benchmark scripts and can run a dedicated pre-prod load test during the POC.
[03:57] Jordan: on contractual items — we have an SLA exhibit, a security addendum, and a pricing schedule. i'll attach links: security pack (https://redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf), sla-exhibit (link to draft), pricing-sheet (internal link).
[04:10] Laura: do you have SOC2 Type II and iso attestation?
[04:14] Jordan: yes, SOC2 Type II report available and ISO 27001 in progress; i'll share the SOC2 and our cert summary.
[04:21] Amira: for the DPA, we will likely ask for a 30 day retention default and ability to request deletion earlier — is that ok?
[04:28] Jordan: yes, we can propose deletion windows and a custom retention schedule in the DPA exhibit.
[04:34] Daniel: any data residency constraints? we operate primarily in EU and need EU residency for certain datasets.
[04:41] Priya: we support region selection for hosted or Dedicated placement; for strict EU residency Private deployment in EU region or on-prem will meet that requirement.
[04:50] Laura: procurement also asked about insurance requirements — do you carry cyber liability?
[04:55] Jordan: yes we carry cyber insurance — details in the compliance pack.
[05:00] Michael: last technical Q — are there any known limitations with model quantization when you do on-prem? we want to keep quality guarantees.
[05:07] Priya: quantization can change small generation characteristics, we'll recommend specific quant profiles per model and run quality checks in the POC. recommendations will be in the Optimize report.
[05:17] Jordan: ok, summary / next steps — we'll: 1) send MSA + DPA + SOC2 by 2026-11-13, 2) Priya shares POC runbook and benchmark scripts by 2026-11-12, 3) schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-11-16, 4) customer to return redlines and confirm procurement timeline.
[05:33] Laura: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:35] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[05:38] (call ends)

Notes: minor transcription errors likely in technical terms "K V cache" instead of KV cache, vendor names sometimes transcribed as CloudProviderX etc. References: security-pack link above, draft SLA exhibit (internal), pricing sheet (internal spreadsheet).
